evidence.t: Deer here are black tailed deer, the coast form of mule deer: the synopsis calls them "mule (black-tailed) deer" (99%, Rule Book: Region 2 Lower Mainland).
Mule deer winter range u-2-005 unit G75-11-RO (official), right here. Counts from October.
Cutblock harvested 2017 (9 years old), right here.
Habitat zone Coastal Western Hemlock (CWHdm3): coast forest, where black tailed deer are among the most common large mammals (95%) and use logged ground often (80%) (lesson: Wet forests).
W facing slope, 18 degrees: sun melts snow first.
Private fields 360 m SW: deer feed on field edges (fields are private).
Black bear: young cutblocks and burns grow berries in late summer and fall (Tip).

flags.t: Route crosses private land (ParcelMap BC, updated 2026-09-27): get permission first or go around.
Private land 360 m SW: no shooting within 100 m (109 yd) of an occupied house or farm building (synopsis page 10, 99%).

plan: Drive: from Resort Municipality of Whistler, about 55 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 49.73851, -123.07427, where the truck road ends (N Ring Creek FSR); unload the ATV (all terrain vehicle). Map links below.
Ride: 1.9 km on park access by ATV (all terrain vehicle) or 4x4 on rough road, estimate. Then walk 120 m N, climb about 1 m.
Hunt: deer, Sept, Oct, Nov, Dec (season rows). Watch the edge of the 2017 cutblock (right here) at first and last light. Sit above it with the wind in your face and glass (Tip).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 165 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 2-7, Region 2. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-09-27, closures 2026-10-16.
R3A-deer-atv-0002.popWhy: Popular (more hunters): MU 2-7: about 310 hunter days a year for mule deer and white tailed deer (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.31 days per square km, middle third of BC MUs; access: close to pavement, a town or a rec site. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

tags.label: Good for 2
tags.why: Cover edge here (cutblock or burn): one hunter sits at a crossing or glasses, the other walks the edge slowly with the wind at their back toward the stander. Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).

tags.label: Good solo
tags.why: Short pack out: 0.1 km and about 1 m of climb from the parking (Tip). Cell coverage is not in the data: leave a trip plan and carry SOS or a satellite messenger (lesson: Bush safety).

R3A-deer-drive-0006.recDirections: Drive North from Squamish on HWY 99 for approx. 11km; Watch for the sign on the HWY directing you to turn off. Turn right onto the Cheekeye Forest Service Road. Travel approx. 2.5km, Cat Lake parking lot is on the right hand side. Please note for travellers headed Southbound after your stay, left hand turns are prohibited onto HWY 99 from the Cheekeye FSR. Turn right to head northbound on HWY 99 for ~300m and turn left into Brohm Lake Day Use Parking Lot to turn around and rejoin HWY 99 South.
